about: A map of Jarvis's own code as it stood at this commit: the major parts, the files each part owns, the module to start reading for each, and the suites and documents that go with it. It names code; it does not hold code and it runs nothing.

architecture.title: The backend on this PC
architecture.sentence: A Python program on the owner's Windows PC serves the page and the apps at 127.0.0.1, and every feature is one module loaded by that program.

architecture.title: The models in Ollama
architecture.sentence: The AI models run in Ollama on this PC's two graphics cards; the backend reaches them over loopback and nothing private leaves the machine.

architecture.title: The Tauri desktop shell
architecture.sentence: A Rust window around the HUD page shows the face, the cards and the Brain, and holds the pairing token out of the page's reach.

architecture.title: The Android client
architecture.sentence: A Jetpack Compose app on the owner's phone talks to the same backend over Tailscale or NordVPN Meshnet, two private device-to-device networks, never a public tunnel.

architecture.title: The public repository and its pipeline
architecture.sentence: The code is the public GitHub repository darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis; a change becomes a pull request, GitHub Actions runs the checks, and the patch stack installs the merged tree on the PC.

subsystems.title: Approvals and the gate
subsystems.purpose: Every action that needs permission becomes one approval card, decided by the owner on the PC, with a plain reason and no way to batch a yes.

The words on an approval card, in one place: its title, its short summary, its label, its button order, and what Jarvis SAYS about a card during a spoken question.
Catching "I've done it" when nothing was done ("Smarter answers", 2026-09-28).
